articles.title: Telehealth companies keep exposing their customers' medical data. What should they do?
articles.desc: It's not hard to explain why business is booming for telehealth companies.
articles.content: Telehealth companies keep exposing their customers' medical data. What should they do? 2 special weather statements in effect for Carroll and Grayson Regions Telehealth companies keep exposing their customers' medical data. What should they do? is easy to explain: Instead of calling a doctor, booking an appointment and hoping to eventually get a prescription, you can log onto an app or website and have launched with the promise of quick, convenient access to drugs for ADHD, sexual dysfunction, anxiety, weight loss and more. Increasingly, though, government regulators are accusing these companies of , including disclosing their customers’ health data, signing them up for hard-to-cancel subscriptions and bypassing real-time consultations with doctors. engaged in all of those tactics, running afoul of U.S. consumer protection laws. Hims has disputed the government's claims, calling them “an effort to generate headlines at our expense.” In recent years, FTC officials have filed similar cases against more than a half-dozen telehealth companies, including online therapy provider . In both cases, regulators said the companies shared users' health data with online platforms such as Meta and Google, without getting permission. Experts say part of the problem is that federal laws that govern the handling of health information generally don’t apply to telehealth companies. “There’s an entire universe of companies collecting huge amounts of consumer health data every day that aren’t covered by our current health sector-specific laws,” said Andrew Crawford, an attorney with the nonprofit Center for Democracy and Technology. Here are some things to know before signing up for a telehealth service: Don’t expect to actually talk to a physician Nearly all telehealth visits begin with a questionnaire in which users provide details about their medical history and possible medications they’re interested in. According to the FTC’s lawsuit, Hims customers were automatically enrolled and billed for recurring prescriptions with “virtually no opportunity to review the provider’s recommended treatment.” Researchers have documented similar practices across the industry, even for injectable weight-loss drugs that typically require a physical exam and other precautions before beginning treatment. A recent analysis of nearly 50 telehealth companies selling found that less than a third actually required any real-time video or audio consultation with a physician. In some cases, the prescriptions were approved within minutes. “What we saw overwhelmingly was that it was incredibly easy to get access to the GLP-1s,” said Dr. Reshma Ramachandran of Yale University, who led the study. “Most of the time, the prescription was automatically sent, without even an opportunity to stop the dispensing.” The lack of a real-time conversation means many patients aren’t getting the type of care recommended by medical societies that prescribe GLP-1s, including discussions about weight-loss goals, past efforts and eating disorders. Only a little more than half the websites had a question about eating disorders — which GLP-1 drugs can induce or worsen — on their intake questionnaires, the researchers found. Your data may be shared with advertisers, social media companies and others Americans often assume that any personal health information they share is protected by HIPAA, the that governs the handling of medical information. But the law generally only applies to specific types of health businesses, including medical offices, hospitals and insurers, not telehealth companies offering prescriptions, counseling, DNA tests and other online services. Privacy experts say that legal gap is one reason companies continue to disclose sensitive health information to advertisers and search engines. “There isn’t a clear federal law saying: ‘Don’t do this,’” said Justin Brookman, Consumer Reports' director of technology policy. “There’s just a body of soft law and settled cases with the FTC

articles.title: Erode Corporation plans drone-based mapping
articles.desc: Erode Corporation launches drone mapping project for detailed 2D and 3D city maps to enhance urban planning and infrastructure.
articles.content: Erode Corporation plans drone-based mapping - The Hindu Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Erode Corporation plans drone-based mapping - September 19, 2026 05:38 pm IST - ERODE The Corporation has initiated steps to prepare detailed 2D and 3D maps of the entire area of the Corporation using drones and modern surveying technology in Erode in Tamil Nadu. | Photo Credit: GOVARTHAN M. The Erode City Municipal Corporation has initiated steps to prepare detailed 2D and 3D maps of the entire corporation area using drones and modern surveying technology. The project is aimed at improving urban planning, civic administration and infrastructure development by creating a comprehensive Geographic Information System (GIS) database of the city. Under the project, aerial surveys will be carried out using drones equipped with cameras and Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) technology. The data collected will be used to prepare detailed maps of buildings, roads, bridges, water bodies, trees, open spaces and other important features in the city. The exercise will also help the Corporation create a digital database of properties and public utilities. The information is expected to assist officials in planning infrastructure projects, monitoring civic assets and taking up development works based on accurate ground data. The initiative is part of efforts to strengthen e-governance and promote the use of GIS technology by urban local bodies. A three-dimensional (3D) model of the city, covering buildings and other major structures, will also be prepared. The data will provide a common digital platform for various departments of the Corporation and support the implementation and monitoring of urban development schemes. The Corporation has proposed engaging a qualified agency to undertake the aerial survey, data collection and preparation of the maps. The completed datasets and related information will be handed over to the Corporation for use in future planning and administration. The project is expected to provide the civic body with an updated picture of the city’s physical infrastructure and help improve decision-making and service delivery. The Corporation has floated a tender for the project with October 6, 2026 as the deadline for online submission of documents. articles.title: El Paso County Commissioners Rack Up $234K Travel Tab From Austin to Hawaii
articles.desc: El Paso County commissioners spent nearly $234,000 on travel since 2022, records show, with David Stout's tab topping $126,000 amid budget strain.
articles.content: El Paso County Commissioners' $234K Travel Spending Since 2022 El Paso County Commissioners Rack Up $234K Travel Tab From Austin to Hawaii El Paso County Commissioners Court — County Governing Body El Paso County commissioners and the county judge have spent nearly $234,000 on travel since fiscal year 2022, with trips stretching from Austin and Washington, D.C. to Las Vegas, Hawaii and Taiwan. Precinct 2 Commissioner David Stout alone accounted for more than $126,000 of that total between fiscal year 2022 and May 2026, according to records reviewed as part of the analysis. The figures come from nearly five years of travel and expense records obtained through a Texas Public Information Act request, as reported by . The county's fiscal year runs October 1 through September 30, and the outlet's review covers spending from fiscal year 2022 through May 2026. Stout's travel included a May 2026 trip to Hawaii for a conference, while commissioners as a group traveled frequently to Washington, D.C., Denver, Las Vegas and Austin. Beyond Stout, the report shows Commissioner Iliana Holguin spent nearly $30,000 on travel over that span, County Judge Ricardo Samaniego spent about $28,000, Precinct 4 Commissioner Sergio Coronado spent almost $23,000, former Commissioner Carlos Leon spent about $10,381 during his final 39 months in office, and Commissioner Jackie Butler spent more than $16,412 during her first 20 months in office. El Paso County's travel and professional education spending was also part of the analysis. Stout's Travel Peaked in Fiscal Year 2024 Stout's annual travel spending climbed from $13,425 in fiscal year 2022 to $29,701 in fiscal year 2023, then peaked at $37,725 in fiscal year 2024 — a year that included nine trips to Austin alone. He had spent more than $18,000 through May 2026 before losing his Democratic primary reelection bid on March 3, 2026. Stout told the outlet that travel helps county officials advocate for El Paso and bring back ideas from other jurisdictions. His trips included a May 2024 visit to Yosemite for the National Association of Counties Western Interstate Region conference, which cost taxpayers about $3,559, and a Las Vegas trip for the National Association of Latino Elected and Appointed Officials conference that cost more than $3,250. A conference trip to Maui cost taxpayers about $4,800 and earned Stout 7,024 Southwest Airlines Rapid Rewards points on the taxpayer-funded flight. Stout said the county paid only for hotel nights tied to the Western Interstate Region conference, and that when family members, friends or other non-county personnel joined him on taxpayer-funded trips, he covered their expenses himself. He was accompanied by at least one county staff member on the Hawaii trip. Under Texas Penal Code § 39.02(d), frequent flyer miles and other travel discount awards earned during official public business are explicitly excluded from being considered government property under state criminal misuse laws, according to the . That means Stout's accrual of airline points on a taxpayer-funded trip, while drawing public scrutiny, is not a crime under state law — though the county's policy on travel rewards, airline miles or other loyalty benefits earned on county business is not addressed here. Samaniego's Taiwan Trip and a Reversed Donation Vote Samaniego's travel included a six-day economic development trip to Taiwan in 2025, tied to Taiwanese cloud infrastructure provider Wiwynn's manufacturing investment in Socorro. The trip initially cost taxpayers about $9,200 in March 2025 and included roughly $7,855 in business-class airfare. Commissioners court voted unanimously on March 10, 2025, to allow Samaniego to accept private donations for the trip, then reversed that decision in a 4-0 vote a week later, on March 17, 2025. articles.title: AI “Actor” Tilly Norwood Glitches Out During Interview, Starts Rambling in Chinese
articles.desc: "You seem to be speaking Chinese completely randomly for no reason." The post AI “Actor” Tilly Norwood Glitches Out During Interview, Starts Rambling in Chinese appeared first on Futurism .
articles.content: AI "Actor" Tilly Norwood Glitches Out During Interview, Starts Rambling in Chinese It won’t bag “her” any awards, but the AI “actor” Till Norwood just put in the performance of a lifetime. — also deserving of scare quotes, but we’re trying to show some restraint here — with British political commentator Piers Morgan, the smiling AI persona, with her uncanny gaze permanently fixed at some indeterminate point that’s somewhere not quite the center of the camera, appeared to severely glitch out before suddenly ranting in Chinese. When Morgan’s human guest, the actor Tom Conti, asks if the other actors in Norwood’s films are real or AI, the AI didn’t seem to understand his question and gave a hard-to-follow answer. Conti’s poses the question again, and gets an unexpected response. “They’re all digital twins, just like me,” Norwood began to explain. “It’s a hybrid production which means…” She stops, still smiling. Then, without missing a beat, proceeds to start rambling in Mandarin. Both Morgan and Conti look baffled, and the AI keeps blustering before it’s finally cut off. “You seem to be speaking Chinese completely randomly for no reason. Why did you do that?” Morgan asks. “Oh, my apologies, it seems I had a little hiccup there,” Norwood replies, adding that sometimes her “wires get crossed.” Morgan presses. “How often do you start talking in Chinese when you’re talking to two English people?” (Conti is Scottish.) “Honestly not often at all, that was a bit of a curveball, even for me,” the AI says. Norwood — or should we say the company behind it, Particle 6 Productions — has been on something of a media blitz lately. Last week, it did with the AI creation, which was widely followed up with softball interviews of their own.) Unexpectedly launching into a rant into a different language is far from its only gaffe, but it’s probably Norwood’s most embarrassing. Still, in an , Norwood did have the temerity to assert that AI-generated movies are good for the environment. She also countered that “all lives matter” — a slogan used by the right to dismiss systemic safety issues faced by minorities — when asked if Black lives do. If this is the future of Hollywood, it’s reassuring to know that the press junket faux pas isn’t going away, at least. articles.title: This Dolphin Steals from Fish for Its Meals
articles.desc: Putting a dent in dolphins’ reputation as the “good guys of the sea” The post This Dolphin Steals from Fish for Its Meals appeared first on Nautilus .
articles.content: This Dolphin Steals from Fish for Its Meals - Nautilus This Dolphin Steals from Fish for Its Meals Putting a dent in dolphins’ reputation as the “good guys of the sea” Because dolphins are highly social and have natural, smile-like jaw shapes, they’re . But dolphins are predators, and like other predators, they go to great lengths to procure animal meat. In fact, in a recent study published in , researchers based in Florida and Australia discovered that common bottlenose dolphins ) will not only eat fish but also steal their meals. The researchers observed the behavior of a dolphin in shallow waters on the southern Great Barrier Reef over a four-year period, both through snorkeling and video. Overall, the dolphin stole food 11 times. He employed a novel strategy of chasing bigeye trevally fishes ( ) until they regurgitated their food and then consumed the morsels. His kleptoparasitic (food-stealing) behavior was facilitated by continual echolocation clicks and low-frequency vocalizations, which may have heightened the trevallys’ sense of fear. “We observed him repeating this behavior over several years which suggests he may have learnt to target the fish with the fullest bellies, providing the most rewarding meals,” explained co-lead author Asia Haines, a marine biologist at the University of the Sunshine Coast in a This male dolphin, nicknamed “Bubbles,” always foraged alone, an atypical behavior since common bottlenose dolphins tend to hunt in groups, working collectively to corral schools of fishes within striking distance. The researchers theorize that given that Bubbles was by himself, he may have needed an alternative strategy that required less energy than catching fish. The bigeye trevally are the perfect hosts for such a kleptoparasite, as they gather in large concentrations, offering a predictable source of regurgitated food. Do Dolphins Have Conversations? We Still Can’t Say Dolphins are infamously smart, and Bubbles’ “behavior does demonstrate the species’ adaptability and flexibility when it comes to foraging,” according to co-lead study author Romney Edwards-Francis, a doctoral student at the University of the Sunshine Coast. Bubbles had frequented the area around Lady Elliot Island where the study was conducted since at least 2017. Given that he wasn’t observed directly eating the trevally, despite dolphins consuming them at other sites, the researchers concluded that Bubbles had learned his unique feeding approach. It might not be fine dining, but it’s obviously kept him well fed. and a science writer based in Alexandria, Virginia. articles.title: investingLive Americas market news wrap: Bonds slump again, yen rate check adds intrigue after BOJ
articles.desc: US industrial production 0.0% versus 0.3% expected Kansas City Fed's Schmid: recent data suggest inflation trending above 3% Japan conducted an FX rate check earlier - report How have interest rate expectations changed after this week's events? Markets: Gold up $41 to $4381 US 10-year yields up 6 bp
articles.content: US industrial production 0.0% versus 0.3% expected Kansas City Fed's Schmid: recent data suggest inflation trending above 3% Japan conducted an FX rate check earlier - report How have interest rate expectations changed after this week's events? Markets: Gold up $41 to $4381 US 10-year yields up 6 bps to 5.01% WTI crude oil down $1.66 to $95.56 AUD leads, JPY lags US stocks finish flat Bitcoin up 6% The newsflow was fairly light in North America but the market moves weren't. Eyes remained on bonds in the aftermath of the FOMC decision and the tug-of-war continued, this time pushing yields back close to 19-year highs. The front end stepped up again, with 2s to 4.75%, the highest since 2024 and close enough to 10s to start thinking about yield curve inversion if the Fed meets the 2-3 further rate hikes priced in. The pressure on the short end helped to lift USD/JPY but that ran into trouble at a high of 158.05. That's when the BOJ did a rate check, according to a Nikkei report. The BOJ hiked rates earlier but the 7-2 vote suggested it might be done sooner rather than later. With that Japanese stock markets put in a strong day as well. Elsewhere in FX, the moves were modest with the commodity currencies and the euro largely flat ont he day. The pound rebounded from the BOE decision but that came after six days of selling. Gold found some buyers despite rising yields in a breakdown in the usual correlation and a positive sign. More impressive was bitcoin up 6% to $81K and ethereum up 7%. Bitcoin withstood the Clarity Act mess and some think it's not dead but the reaction could also indicate underlying demand that was waiting for the dust to settle. It's impressive in any case as Clarity Act headlines are now an upside risk. Have a great weekend. This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.
